translation_literal: Someone might say: all virtues were perfect in Our Lady, so perfect detachment must have been in her. If detachment is higher than humility, why did she praise her humility and not her detachment when she said, 'He has regarded the humility of his handmaid'? Why not: he has regarded the detachment of his handmaid? I answer: detachment and humility are in God, so far as we may speak of virtues in God. Know this: loving humility brought God to incline into human nature, while detachment stood immovable in itself when he became human — as it stood when he created heaven and earth. And because our Lord, wishing to become human, stood immovable in his detachment, Our Lady knew well that he desired the same of her, and that in this matter he regarded her humility, not her detachment. So she stood immovable in her detachment and praised her humility, not her detachment. Had she so much as thought with one word of her detachment — 'he regarded my detachment' — that detachment would have been troubled and would no longer have been whole and perfect, for a going-out would have occurred. No going-out can be so small that detachment remains unblemished in it. So you have the reason she praised humility and not detachment. Therefore the prophet said: I will be silent and hear what my God and Lord may speak *in* me — as if to say: if God would speak to me, let him come in here; I will not go out.
commentary:
The Marian puzzle teaches a discipline of silence about the highest state. Humility can be *named* because naming it is congruent with its outward bow; detachment cannot be named without performing the very going-out that ruins it. Mary's wisdom is double: she keeps detachment immovable while offering humility as the speakable surface God regards for the Incarnation's work. The prophet's line seals the practice: do not go out to fetch God; be silent so God can speak *in*. The contested pastoral implication is sharp: talking about one's detachment, advertising one's emptiness, or making a spiritual brand of non-attachment is already the fall. Existentially: the deepest work may be the one you refuse to narrate.

Key Terms

**unbewegelich (MHG)** — "immovable." God's and Mary's detachment share this quality; motion toward creatures (even verbal) is the threat.

**ûzganc (MHG)** — "going-out." Even a word of self-reference about detachment counts as exit.

**in mich / hin ûz (MHG)** — "into me" / "outward." The spatial grammar of contemplation: God enters; the soul does not exit to seek.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Bhagavad Gītā 2.47–2.48 (act without clinging to fruits / even to the act's spiritual credit):** Both warn that claiming the fruit — including the fruit of being detached — rebinds.
*Divergence:* The Gītā keeps the field of action (karma); Eckhart's silence is about not exiting the ground even by holy speech.

**Laozi / Tao Te Ching (the Way that can be named is not the constant Way):** Both treat naming the highest as a betrayal of it.
*Divergence:* Daoist namelessness is cosmic; Eckhart's unnameable detachment is a heart-state ordered to personal divine presence.
practice: For the rest of today, do not speak or write about your spiritual state — no progress report, no humility performance, no 'I'm working on detachment.' When the urge to narrate arises, be silent for three breaths and listen inward as if God might speak there.
sanskrit_devanagari: Nû möhte ein mensche sprechen: nû wâren doch alle tugende volkomenlîche in unser vrouwen, und alsô muoste ouch volkomeniu abegescheidenheit in ir sîn. Ist nû abegescheidenheit hœher dan dêmüeticheit, war umbe ruomte sich danne unser vrouwe ir dêmüeticheit und niht ir abegescheidenheit, dô si sprach: 'quia respexit dominus humilitatem ancillae suae', daz ist: 'er sach ane die dêmüeticheit sîner diernen', - war umbe ensprach si niht: er sach ane die abegescheidenheit sîner diernen? Des antwürte ich alsô und spriche, daz in gote ist abegescheidenheit und dêmüeticheit, als verre wir tugende von gote gesprechen mügen. Nû solt dû wizzen, daz diu minnebære dêmüeticheit got dâ zuo brâhte, daz er sich neigete in menschlîche natûre, und stuont abegescheidenheit unbewegelich in ir selber, dô er mensche wart, als si tete, dô er himelrîche und ertrîche beschuof, als ich dir her nâch sagen wil. Und wan unser herre, dô er mensche werden wolte, unbewegelich stuont an sîner abegescheidenheit, dô weste unser vrouwe wol, daz er des selben ouch von ir begerte und daz er in der sache anesach ir dêmüeticheit und niht ir abegescheidenheit. Dâ von stuont si unbewegelich in ir abegescheidenheit und ruomte sich ir dêmüeticheit und niht ir abegescheidenheit. Und hæte si niuwan gedâht mit einem worte ir abegescheidenheit, daz si gesprochen hæte: er sach ane mîne abegescheidenheit, dâ mite wære diu abegescheidenheit betrüebet worden und wære niht ganz noch volkomen gewesen, wan dâ wære ein ûzganc geschehen. Sô enmac kein ûzganc sô kleine gesîn, in dem diu abegescheidenheit müge âne mâsen blîben. Und alsô hâst dû die sache, war umbe sich unser vrouwe ruomte ir dêmüeticheit und niht ir abegescheidenheit. Dâ von sprach der wîssage: 'audiam, quid loquatur in me dominus deus', daz ist gesprochen: 'ich wil' swîgen und wil 'hœren, waz mîn got und mîn herre in mich rede', als ob er spræche: wil got ze mir reden, sô kome her in mich, ich enwil niht hin ûz.

unit_label: Empty of Creatures, Full of God
title: Empty of Creatures, Full of God
sanskrit_devanagari: Nû maht dû vrâgen, waz abegescheidenheit sî, wan si als gar edel an ir selber ist? Hie solt dû wizzen, daz rehtiu abegescheidenheit niht anders enist, wan daz der geist alsô unbewegelich stande gegen allen zuovellen liebes und leides, êren, schanden und lasters als ein blîgîn berc unbewegelich ist gegen einem kleinen winde. Disiu unbewegelîchiu abegescheidenheit bringet den menschen in die grœste glîcheit mit gote. Wan daz got ist got, daz hât er von sîner unbewegelîchen abegescheidenheit, und von der abegescheidenheit hât er sîne lûterkeit und sîne einvalticheit und sîne unwandelbærkeit. Und dâ von, sol der mensche gote glîch werden, als verre als ein crêatûre glîcheit mit gote gehaben mac, daz muoz geschehen mit abegescheidenheit. Diu ziuhet danne den menschen in lûterkeit und von der lûterkeit in einvalticheit und von der einvalticheit in unwandelbærkeit, und diu dinc bringent eine glîcheit zwischen gote und dem menschen; und diu glîcheit muoz beschehen in gnâden, wan diu gnâde ziuhet den menschen von allen zîtlîchen dingen und liutert in von allen zergenclîchen dingen. Und dû solt wizzen: lære sîn aller crêatûre ist gotes vol sîn, und vol sîn aller crêatûre ist gotes lære sîn.
sanskrit_iast: Middle High German — see Original.
translation_literal: Now you may ask what detachment is, since it is so noble in itself. Know this: true detachment is nothing other than for the spirit to stand as immovable against whatever may befall it of joy and sorrow, honor, shame, and disgrace, as a mountain of lead stands immovable before a little wind. This immovable detachment brings a person into the greatest equality with God. For that God is God, he has from his immovable detachment; and from detachment he has his purity, his simplicity, and his unchangeability. Therefore if a human being is to become equal with God — so far as a creature can have equality with God — it must happen through detachment. Detachment then draws one into purity, and from purity into simplicity, and from simplicity into unchangeability, and these produce an equality between God and the human being; and that equality must come about in grace, for grace draws one from all temporal things and purifies from all transient things. And you must know: to be empty of all creatures is to be full of God, and to be full of all creatures is to be empty of God.
commentary:
Here Eckhart defines the virtue by a physics of immovability. The lead mountain does not refuse the wind by fighting it; it is simply too dense to be swayed. Equality with God is not moral imitation but participation in God's own detachment — the purity, simplicity, and unchangeability by which God *is* God. The ladder (purity → simplicity → unchangeability) is a phenomenology of emptying, and Eckhart insists the equality is *in grace*, not self-manufacture. The final maxim is the treatise in one line: creature-full equals God-empty; creature-empty equals God-full. The contested pastoral reading of Stoic calm is refused: this is not indifference as armor but vacancy as hospitality. Existentially: inventory what currently "fills" the heart; each occupancy is a displacement of God.

Key Terms

**blîgîn berc (MHG)** — "lead mountain." Image of density against trivial force; detachment's strength is mass of emptiness, not willpower clenched.

**einvalticheit (MHG)** — "simplicity, single-foldedness." Not naivety; undividedness — the opposite of a heart split among creatures.

**lære sîn / vol sîn (MHG)** — "to be empty" / "to be full." Zero-sum occupancy: creatures and God do not cohabit as equals in the same receptive place.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Īśāvāsya Upaniṣad 1 (the Lord's filling / renunciation):** Both couple fullness of the Absolute with a releasing of grasping.
*Divergence:* The Īśā holds enjoyment-with-renunciation in the world; Eckhart's maxim is starker about mutual exclusion in the heart's occupancy.

**Plotinus VI.9 (union by stripping to simplicity):** Both ascend by simplification toward the unchangeable.
*Divergence:* Plotinus's One is beyond being and intellect; Eckhart's God remains the personal giver who occupies the emptied heart by grace.
insight: Here Eckhart defines the virtue by a physics of immovability.
practice: Evening review: list what occupied your heart today (people, fears, ambitions, screens). For each, say quietly: this filled me; therefore God was crowded out. Then sit two minutes empty — not pushing contents away violently, just not feeding them — and notice the different density.

unit_label: God Does Not Begin to Love in Time
title: God Does Not Begin to Love in Time
thesis: Eckhart protects God's immutability without voiding prayer.
source_excerpt: Know that God has stood in this immovable detachment from everlasting and still stands. translation_literal: Know that God has stood in this immovable detachment from everlasting and still stands. When God created heaven and earth and all creatures, that affected his immovable detachment as little as if no creature had ever been made. Further: all the prayer and good works a person can perform in time move God's detachment as little as if no prayer or good work ever happened in time — and God is never the gentler or more inclined toward someone than if that prayer or work had never been done. Further still: when the Son in the Godhead wished to become human and became human and suffered, that affected God's immovable detachment as little as if he had never become human. You might say: then all prayer and good works are wasted, since God is not moved by them — and yet people say God wants to be asked for everything. Understand, if you can: in his first eternal glance God saw all things as they would happen — when and how he would create, when the Son would become human and suffer, the least prayer and work anyone would do, and which devotion he would hear. He saw that tomorrow you will call on him earnestly; he will not hear that prayer *tomorrow*, for he has heard it in his eternity before you ever became human. If your prayer lacks earnestness, he does not refuse you *now*; he has refused you in his eternity. So God works nothing newly; everything is already wrought beforehand. Thus God always stands in immovable detachment — and yet prayer and good works are not lost: whoever does well is well rewarded, whoever does ill is rewarded accordingly. As Augustine says: God forbid anyone should say God loves someone in time, for with him nothing is past or future; he loved all the saints before the world was made. When in time he shows what he has regarded in eternity, people think God has turned a new love toward them; yet when he seems angry or gracious, *we* are changed and *he* remains unchangeable — as sunlight hurts sick eyes and helps healthy ones, while the sunlight itself remains unchangeable.
commentary:
Eckhart protects God's immutability without voiding prayer. The contested synthesis: temporally, nothing you do *begins* a new divine attitude; eternally, your earnest prayer is already included in the first glance that sees all. Prayer is not lever-pulling on a changeable God; it is alignment with what eternity has already regarded. The Augustine sun image relocates all drama of divine mood into the creature's changing receptivity. Existentially: pray earnestly without the superstition that you are updating God; let the practice change *you* into the one who can bear the light.

Key Terms

**êwiger anblik (MHG)** — "eternal glance." God's single regard in which all temporal events are seen at once.

**unwandelbære (MHG)** — "unchangeable." Applied to God; change is predicated of us.

**vorgewürket (MHG)** — "already wrought beforehand." Denies novelty in God without denying the moral seriousness of acts.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Bhagavad Gītā 9–11 (the cosmic form / acts within an already-complete divine field):** Both place human action inside a totality that is not surprised by time.
*Divergence:* The Gītā keeps a personal Lord who reciprocates devotion within līlā; Eckhart stresses that reciprocity never implies temporal change in God.

**Know Yourself / Balyānī (no before or after with the One):** Both refuse temporal predicates of the Absolute.
*Divergence:* The Sufi treatise often dissolves the creature more absolutely; Eckhart keeps prayer, works, and reward language while relocating their efficacy.
practice: Pray one sincere request today. Afterward, sit with this: it is not that God will decide later; eternity has already regarded this. Ask only — am I becoming someone who can receive what the light already is?
sanskrit_devanagari: Nû solt dû wizzen, daz got in dirre unbewegelîchen abegescheidenheit ist êwelten gestanden und noch stât, und solt wizzen: dô got himelrîche und ertrîche beschuof und alle crêatûre, daz gienc sîne unbewegelîche abegescheidenheit als wênic ane, als ob nie crêatûre geschaffen wære. Ich spriche ouch mêr: allez daz gebet und guotiu werk, diu der mensche in der zît mac gewürken, daz gotes abegescheidenheit alsô wênic dâ von beweget wirt, als ob niendert gebet noch guotez werk in der zît beschæhe, und enwirt got niemer deste milter noch deste geneigeter gegen dem menschen, dan ob er daz gebet oder diu guoten werk niemer gewürhte. Ich spriche ouch mêr: dô der sun in der gotheit mensche werden wolte und wart und die marter leit, daz gienc die unbewegelîche abegescheidenheit gotes alsô wênic ane, als ob er nie mensche worden wære. Nû möhtest dû sprechen: sô hœre ich wol, allez gebet und alliu guotiu werk sint verlorn, wan sich got ir niht anenimet, daz in ieman dâ mite bewegen müge, und sprichet man doch: got wil umbe alliu dinc gebeten werden. Hie solt dû mich wol merken und rehte verstân, ob dû maht, daz got in sînem êrsten êwigen anblicke - ob wir einen êrsten anblik dâ nemen solten -, alliu dinc anesach, als sie beschehen solten, und sach in dem selben anblicke, wanne und wie er die crêatûre schepfen wolte und wanne der sun mensche werden wolte und lîden solte; er sach ouch daz minste gebet und guote werk, daz ieman solte tuon, und sach ane, welhez gebet und andâht er erhœren wolte oder solte; er sach, daz dû in morgen wilt mit ernste aneruofen und biten, und daz aneruofen und gebet enwil got niht morgen erhœren, wan er hât ez erhœret in sîner êwicheit, ê dû ie mensche würde. Enist aber dîn gebet niht endelich und âne ernst, sô enwil dir got niht nû versagen, wan er hât dir in sîner êwicheit versaget. Und alsô hât got in sînem êrsten êwigen anblicke alliu dinc anegesehen, und got würket nihtes niht von niuwem, wan ez ist allez ein vorgewürket dinc [1]. Und alsô stât got alle zît in sîner unbewegelîchen abegescheidenheit, und enist doch dar umbe der liute gebet und guotiu werk niht verlorn; wan der wol tuot, dem wirt ouch wol gelônet, der übel tuot, dem wirt ouch dar nâch gelônet. Disen sin redet sant Augustînus in dem fünften buoche von der drîvalticheit in dem jüngesten capitel und sprichet alsô: »Deus autem« etc., daz ist als vil gesprochen: »nû enwelle got, daz ieman spreche, daz got ieman zîtlîche minne, wan bî im enist nihtes niht verloufen und ouch nihtes niht künftic und hât alle heiligen geminnet, ê diu werlt ie wart geschaffen, als er sie versehen hât. Und swenne ez kumet in die zît, daz er öuget in der zît, daz er in der êwicheit hât anegesehen, sô wænent die liute, got habe eine niuwe minne an sie geleget; und alsô, sô er zürnet oder etwaz guotes tuot, sô werden wir gewandelt und blîbet er unwandelbære, als der sunnen schîn tuot den siechen ougen wê und den gesunden wol, und blîbet doch der sunnen schîn unwandelbære an im selber.

title: The Door Moves; the Hinge Does Not

translation_literal: Someone might ask: did Christ also have immovable detachment when he said, 'My soul is sorrowful unto death,' and Mary, standing under the cross — of whom so much lament is told? How can this stand with immovable detachment? Know that the masters say there are two persons in every human being: the outer person, which is sensibility, served by the five senses, yet working by the soul's power; and the inner person, which is one's inwardness. A spiritual person who loves God uses the soul's powers in the outer person no further than the five senses necessarily require; and inwardness turns to the senses only as their guide and guardian, lest they use their objects bestially. Whatever powers the soul has beyond what it gives the five senses, it gives entirely to the inner person. Now know: the outer person may be in activity while the inner person stands wholly free and immovable. Christ also had an outer and an inner person, and so did Our Lady; whatever they said of outer matters, they said according to the outer person, while the inner stood in immovable detachment. So Christ spoke when he said his soul was sorrowful unto death; and whatever Our Lady lamented, her inwardness still stood in immovable detachment. Take a likeness: a door opens and closes on a hinge. I liken the outer board of the door to the outer person, and the hinge to the inner person. When the door opens and closes, the outer board moves back and forth, yet the hinge remains in one place, immovable, and is never altered. Just so is it here, if you can take it rightly.
commentary:
Eckhart refuses the false choice between feeling and detachment. Christ's agony and Mary's lament are real in the outer person; they do not require the inner hinge to swing. The contested pastoral error is equating holiness with numbness, or equating emotion with spiritual failure. The door-hinge image is precise engineering: motion at the periphery is compatible with stillness at the axis. Existentially: let the outer life feel, speak, work, and even weep — while asking whether the inner axis is still trying to become a swinging board.

Key Terms

**ûzer mensche / inner mensche (MHG)** — "outer person / inner person." Anthropological dual register, not two selves to war against each other but two functions.

**angel (MHG)** — "hinge." The still pivot; detachment's seat.

**sinnelicheit (MHG)** — "sensibility." Legitimate within need; dangerous when it commandeers all soul-power.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Bhagavad Gītā 2 (the wise one acts while established in the Self):** Both allow full outer engagement without inner displacement.
*Divergence:* The Gītā's steadfastness is often framed as buddhi-yoga in action; Eckhart's hinge is explicitly the seat of *abegescheidenheit* amid pathos.

**Spandakārikā (vibration without loss of the still ground):** Both hold movement and ground together.
*Divergence:* Spanda names the Absolute *as* vibratory; Eckhart keeps a sharper outer/inner split for pastoral clarity.
practice: In the next strong emotion (joy, anger, grief), do not suppress the outer movement. Place attention for thirty seconds on the 'hinge': the awareness that is not identical with the swinging feeling. Whisper: the door moves; the hinge need not.
sanskrit_devanagari: Nû möhte ein mensche sprechen: hâte Kristus ouch unbewegelîche abegescheidenheit, dô er sprach: 'mîn sêle ist betrüebet biz in den tôt' und Marîâ, dô si stuont under dem kriuze, und saget man doch vil von ir klage, - wie mac diz allez bestân mit unbewegelîcher abegescheidenheit? Hie solt dû wizzen, daz die meister sprechent, daz an einem ieglîchen menschen zweierhande menschen sint: der eine heizet der ûzer mensche, daz ist diu sinnelicheit; dúm menschen dienent die fünf sinne und würket doch der ûzer mensche von kraft der sêle. Der ander mensche heizet der inner mensche, daz ist des menschen innerkeit. Nû solt dû wizzen, daz ein geistlîcher mensche, der got minnet, gebrûchet der sêle krefte in dem ûzern menschen niht vürbaz, wan als die fünf sinne ze nôt bedürfen; und diu inwendicheit enkêret sich niht ze den fünf sinnen, wan als verre als si ein wîser und ein leiter ist der fünf sinne und ir hüetet, daz sie niht gebrûchent irs gegenwurfes nâch vihelicheit, als etlîche liute tuont, die lebent nâch ir lîplîcher wollust, als diu vihe tuont, diu âne vernunft sint; und solhe liute heizent eigenlîcher vihe dan liute. Und swaz diu sêle krefte hât über daz si den fünf sinnen gibet, die krefte gibet diu sêle alle dem innern menschen, und sô dúr mensche etwaz hôhes edeles gegenwurfes hât, sô ziuhet si an sich alle die krefte, die si den fünf sinnen gelihen hât, und heizet der mensche sinnelôs und verzücket, wan sîn gegenwurf ist ein vernünftic bilde oder etwaz vernünftiges âne bilde. Doch wizze, daz got von einem ieclîchen geistlîchen menschen muotet, daz er in minne mit allen kreften der sêle. Dâ von sprach er: 'minne dînen got von ganzem herzen'. Nû sint etlîche liute, die verzernt der sêle krefte alzemâle in dem ûzern menschen. Daz sint die liute, die alle ir sinne und vernunft kêrent ûf zergenclich guot, die enwizzen nihtes niht von dem innern menschen. Nû solt dû wizzen, daz der ûzer mensche mac in üebunge sîn, daz doch der inner mensche des genzlîche ledic stât und unbewegelich. Nû was in Kristô ouch ein ûzwendiger mensche und ein inwendiger mensche, und ouch in unser vrouwen; und swaz Kristus und unser vrouwe ie geredeten von ûzern sachen, daz tâten sie nâch dem ûzern menschen, und stuont der inner mensche in einer unbewegelîchen abegescheidenheit. Und alsô redete Kristus, dô er sprach: 'mîn sêle ist betrüebet biz in den tôt', und swaz unser vrouwe klagete, und ander rede, die si tete, sô stuont doch alzît ir inwendicheit in einer unbewegelîchen abegescheidenheit. Und nim des ein ebenbilde: ein tür gât in einem angel ûf und zuo. Nû glîche ich daz ûzer bret an der tür dem ûzern menschen, sô glîche ich den angel dem innern menschen. Sô nû diu tür ûf und zuo gât:, sô wandelt sich daz ûzer bret hin und her, und blîbet doch der angel an einer stat unbewegelich und enwirt dar umbe niemer verwandelt. Ze glîcher wîse ist ez ouch hie, ob dû im kanst rehte tuon.

Und nim des ein ebenbilde: ein tür gât in einem angel ûf und zuo. Nû glîche ich daz ûzer bret an der tür dem ûzern menschen, sô glîche ich den angel dem innern menschen. Sô nû diu tür ûf und zuo gât:, sô wandelt sich daz ûzer bret hin und her, und blîbet doch der angel an einer stat unbewegelich und enwirt dar umbe niemer verwandelt. Ze glîcher wîse ist ez ouch hie, ob dû im kanst rehte tuon.

pratibha_layers.label: Transliteration note
pratibha_layers.body: Middle High German — see Original.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Translation
pratibha_layers.body: Someone might ask: did Christ also have immovable detachment when he said, 'My soul is sorrowful unto death,' and Mary, standing under the cross — of whom so much lament is told? How can this stand with immovable detachment? Know that the masters say there are two persons in every human being: the outer person, which is sensibility, served by the five senses, yet working by the soul's power; and the inner person, which is one's inwardness. A spiritual person who loves God uses the soul's powers in the outer person no further than the five senses necessarily require; and inwardness turns to the senses only as their guide and guardian, lest they use their objects bestially. Whatever powers the soul has beyond what it gives the five senses, it gives entirely to the inner person. Now know: the outer person may be in activity while the inner person stands wholly free and immovable. Christ also had an outer and an inner person, and so did Our Lady; whatever they said of outer matters, they said according to the outer person, while the inner stood in immovable detachment. So Christ spoke when he said his soul was sorrowful unto death; and whatever Our Lady lamented, her inwardness still stood in immovable detachment. Take a likeness: a door opens and closes on a hinge. I liken the outer board of the door to the outer person, and the hinge to the inner person. When the door opens and closes, the outer board moves back and forth, yet the hinge remains in one place, immovable, and is never altered. Just so is it here, if you can take it rightly.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Commentary
pratibha_layers.body:
Eckhart refuses the false choice between feeling and detachment. Christ's agony and Mary's lament are real in the outer person; they do not require the inner hinge to swing. The contested pastoral error is equating holiness with numbness, or equating emotion with spiritual failure. The door-hinge image is precise engineering: motion at the periphery is compatible with stillness at the axis. Existentially: let the outer life feel, speak, work, and even weep — while asking whether the inner axis is still trying to become a swinging board.

Key Terms

**ûzer mensche / inner mensche (MHG)** — "outer person / inner person." Anthropological dual register, not two selves to war against each other but two functions.

**angel (MHG)** — "hinge." The still pivot; detachment's seat.

**sinnelicheit (MHG)** — "sensibility." Legitimate within need; dangerous when it commandeers all soul-power.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Bhagavad Gītā 2 (the wise one acts while established in the Self):** Both allow full outer engagement without inner displacement.
*Divergence:* The Gītā's steadfastness is often framed as buddhi-yoga in action; Eckhart's hinge is explicitly the seat of *abegescheidenheit* amid pathos.

**Spandakārikā (vibration without loss of the still ground):** Both hold movement and ground together.
*Divergence:* Spanda names the Absolute *as* vibratory; Eckhart keeps a sharper outer/inner split for pastoral clarity.

pratibha_layers.label: Practice (Abhyasa)
pratibha_layers.body: In the next strong emotion (joy, anger, grief), do not suppress the outer movement. Place attention for thirty seconds on the 'hinge': the awareness that is not identical with the swinging feeling. Whisper: the door moves; the hinge need not.

Hie solt dû wizzen, daz die meister sprechent, daz an einem ieglîchen menschen zweierhande menschen sint: der eine heizet der ûzer mensche, daz ist diu sinnelicheit; dúm menschen dienent die fünf sinne und würket doch de…

unit_label: The Heart Must Be a Blank Tablet
title: The Heart Must Be a Blank Tablet
thesis: The treatise culminates in a metaphysics of readiness.
source_excerpt: I ask here: what is the object of pure detachment? I answer: neither this nor that is the object of pure detachment. It stands upon a bare nothing [*blôzez niht*], and I will tell you why. Pure detachment stands upon the highest. Now that one stands upon the highest in whom God can work according to his whole will. And though God is almighty, he can work only as he finds readiness or makes it. I say 'or makes it' because of Saint Paul: there God found no readiness, yet prepared him by pouring in grace. So God works according to the readiness he finds. His working differs in a human being and in a stone. Likeness from nature: heat a baking oven and put in doughs of oats, barley, rye, and whea
translation_literal: I ask here: what is the object of pure detachment? I answer: neither this nor that is the object of pure detachment. It stands upon a bare nothing [*blôzez niht*], and I will tell you why. Pure detachment stands upon the highest. Now that one stands upon the highest in whom God can work according to his whole will. And though God is almighty, he can work only as he finds readiness or makes it. I say 'or makes it' because of Saint Paul: there God found no readiness, yet prepared him by pouring in grace. So God works according to the readiness he finds. His working differs in a human being and in a stone. Likeness from nature: heat a baking oven and put in doughs of oats, barley, rye, and wheat — one heat, yet unequal loaves, and the fault is not the heat's but the matter's. Likewise God does not work equally in all hearts; he works as he finds readiness and receptivity. Wherever a heart holds this or that, something in that this-or-that can keep God from working at the highest. Therefore if the heart is to be ready for the highest, it must stand upon a bare nothing — and therein lies the greatest possibility there can be. Will I write on a wax tablet, nothing already written there — however noble — fails to hinder me; if I would write well, I must erase everything, and the tablet never suits writing so well as when nothing at all stands on it. Just so: if God is to write in my heart at the highest, everything that can be called this and that must leave the heart. So stands the detached heart. Therefore God can work there at the highest and according to his uppermost will. Therefore the object of the detached heart is neither this nor that.
commentary:
The treatise culminates in a metaphysics of readiness. Omnipotence does not cancel the need for a fitting receptacle; God works as readiness allows — or as grace creates readiness (Paul). The oven and wax tablet images make the same point: unequal results are often the matter's density, not the heat's failure. *Blôzez niht* is not despairing void but maximal capacity — the greatest *mügelicheit* (possibility). The contested spiritual consumerism of filling the heart with holy this-and-that (images, techniques, identities) is inverted: the highest object is no object. Existentially: erase one noble inscription you keep polishing — a spiritual self-image, a preferred consolation — and leave the tablet blank for an hour.

Key Terms

**blôzez niht (MHG)** — "bare / naked nothing." The objectless ground of detachment; not absence as lack but absence as capacity.

**bereitschaft / enpfenclicheit (MHG)** — "readiness / receptivity." Conditions of divine working in the heart.

**diz noch daz (MHG)** — "neither this nor that." Refusal of every determinate content as the heart's occupying object.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad / Gauḍapāda (turīya beyond waking-dream-sleep contents):** Both point beyond all determinate states to a ground that is not another content.
*Divergence:* Turīya is articulated within an Indic fourfold; Eckhart's bare nothing is the Christian heart cleared for God's writing.

**Pratyabhijñāhṛdayam (Citi resting as herself):** Both end in a state where the Absolute is not an object among objects.
*Divergence:* Recognition reclaims authorship of appearance; Eckhart's blank tablet awaits God's inscription by grace.
practice: Choose one cherished mental inscription (a plan, grievance, spiritual identity). For fifteen minutes, each time it appears, mentally wipe the tablet clean. Do not replace it with a better inscription. End by sitting one minute with nothing written.
sanskrit_devanagari: Nû vrâge ich hie, waz der lûtern abegescheidenheit gegenwurf sî? Dar zuo antwürte ich alsô und spriche, daz weder diz noch daz ist der lûtern abegescheidenheit gegenwurf. Si stât ûf einem blôzen nihte, und sage dir, war umbe daz ist: diu lûteriu abegescheidenheit stât ûf dem hœhsten. Nû stât der ûf dem hœhsten, in dem got nâch allem sînem willen gewürken mac. Nû enmac got niht in allen herzen gewürken nâch allem sînem willen, wan swie daz sî, daz got almehtic ist, sô enmac er doch niht gewürken, wan als er bereitschaft vindet oder machet. Und spriche ich dar umbe 'oder machet' von sant Paulus wegen, wan dâ envant er niht bereitschaft, aber er bereite in mit dem îngiezenne der gnâden. Dâ von spriche ich: got würket dar nâch, als er bereitschaft vindet. Sîn würken ist anders in dem menschen dan in dem steine. Des vinden wir ein glîchnisse in der natûre: sô man einen bakoven heizet und dar în leget einen teic von habern und einen von gersten und einen von roggen und einen von weizen, nû enist niht dan úin hitze in dem ovene und enwürket doch niht glîch in den teigen, wan der ein wirt schœne brôt, der ander wirt rûcher, der dritte noch rûcher. Und daz enist niht der hitze schult, ez ist der materien schult, diu dâ unglîch ist. Ze glîcher wîse sô enwürket got niht glîch in allen herzen; er würket dar nâch, als er bereitschaft und enpfenclicheit vindet. in welhem herzen ist nû diz oder daz, in dem 'diz oder daz' mac etwaz sîn, daz got ûf daz hœhste niht gewürken enmac. Dâ von, sol daz herze bereitschaft haben ûf daz aller hœhste, sô muoz ez stân ûf einem blôzen nihte, und dar inne ist ouch diu grœste mügelicheit, diu gesîn mac. Wan nû daz abegescheiden herze stât ûf dem hœhsten, daz muoz sîn ûf dem nihte, wan dâ ist diu grœste enpfenclicheit inne. Des nim ein glîchnisse in der natûre. Wil ich schrîben an eine wehsîn taveln, sô enmac kein dinc sô edel gesîn, daz an der taveln geschriben stât, ez enirre mich, daz ich niht dar ane geschrîben enmac; und wil ich wol schrîben, sô muoz ich allez daz tilgen und tœten, daz an der taveln stât, und vüeget mir diu tavel niemer als wol ze schrîbenne, als sô nihtes niht an der tavel stât. Ze glîcher wîse: sol got in mîn herze schrîben ûf daz aller hœhste, sô muoz ûz dem herzen komen allez, daz diz und daz geheizen mac, und alsô stât daz abegescheiden herze. Dâ von sô mac got dâ gewürken ûf daz aller hœhste und nâch sînem obersten willen. Dâ von ist des abegescheidenen herzen gegenwurf weder diz noch daz.

unit_label: When All Dharmas Are the Buddha-Dharma
title: When All Dharmas Are the Buddha-Dharma
sanskrit_devanagari:
諸法の仏法なる時節、すなわち、迷悟あり、修行あり、生あり死あり、諸仏あり衆生あり。
万法ともに、われにあらざる時節、まどいなく、さとりなく、諸仏なく衆生なく、生なく滅なし。
仏道もとより豊倹より跳出せるゆえに、生滅あり、迷悟あり、生仏あり。
しかも、かくのごとくなりといえども、華は愛惜にちり、草は棄嫌におうるのみなり。
sanskrit_iast: See Original.
translation_literal: When all dharmas are the Buddha-dharma, then there is delusion and realization, practice, birth and death, buddhas and sentient beings. When the myriad dharmas are without self, there is no delusion, no realization, no buddhas, no beings, no birth, no extinction. The Buddha Way originally leaps clear of abundance and lack; therefore there is birth and extinction, delusion and realization, beings and buddhas. And yet flowers fall amid our longing, and weeds grow amid our loathing.
commentary:
Dōgen opens by holding two truths without neutralizing either: within Buddha-dharma, the whole drama of practice appears; without self, none of that drama obtains as ownership. The contested move is refusing a quietism that denies birth-death while also refusing a dualism that treats practice as acquiring something missing. Flowers fall and weeds grow — longing and aversion do not cease to shape appearance. Existentially: stop waiting for a mood in which practice would be unnecessary; practice is how the Way leaps clear inside abundance and lack.

Key Terms

**現成公案 genjōkōan** — "presencing the absolute matter" / the case actualized now. Not a koan as riddle only; the absolute as this.

**諸法 shohō** — "all dharmas." The total field of phenomena.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Meister Eckhart, *Von Abegescheidenheit* (immovable hinge / emptying):** Both refuse a spirituality of accumulation.
*Divergence:* Eckhart empties for God's occupancy; Dōgen's forgetting is verified by the myriad dharmas.

**Zhuangzi (forgetting the self / useless tree):** Both loosen fixed self-measure.
*Divergence:* Zhuangzi often ends in spontaneous ease; Dōgen binds forgetting to practice-realization.
insight: Dōgen opens by holding two truths without neutralizing either: within Buddha-dharma, the whole drama of practice appears; without self, none of that drama obtains as ownership.
practice: Read the passage once slowly aloud. Sit three minutes without using it to improve a self-story. Then write one sentence: what verified me just now?

Flowers fall and weeds grow — longing and aversion do not cease to shape appearance. Existentially: stop waiting for a mood in which practice would be unnecessary; practice is how the Way leaps clear inside abundance and lack.

**現成公案 genjōkōan** — "presencing the absolute matter" / the case actualized now. Not a koan as riddle only; the absolute as this.

unit_label: Carrying the Self Is Delusion; Being Confirmed by the Myriad Things Is Awakening
title: Carrying the Self Is Delusion; Being Confirmed by the Myriad Things Is Awakening
sanskrit_devanagari:
自己をはこびて万法を修、証するを迷とす。
万法すすみて自己を修、証するは、さとりなり。
迷を大悟するは諸仏なり。
悟に大迷なるは衆生なり。
さらに悟上に得悟する漢あり。
迷中又迷の漢あり。
諸仏の、まさしく諸仏なるときは、自己は諸仏なり、と覚知することをもちいず。
しかあれども、証仏なり。
仏を証しもってゆく。
身心を挙して色を見取し、身心を挙して声を聴取するに、したしく会取すれども、かがみにかげをやどすがごとくにあらず。
水と月とのごとくにあらず。
一方を証するときは一方はくらし。
sanskrit_iast: See Original.
translation_literal: To carry the self forward and practice-realize the myriad dharmas is delusion. That the myriad dharmas come forth and practice-realize the self is awakening. When buddhas are truly buddhas, they do not need to be aware that they are buddhas — yet they are verified buddhas, and they go on verifying buddha.
commentary:
Delusion is self-as-agent pushing into the world; awakening is the world verifying the self. The contested inversion refuses spiritual athleticism as the essence of the path. Buddhas need not self-congratulate as buddhas — verification continues without that identity-claim. Existentially: notice when practice is you carrying a project called enlightenment; soften into being practiced by what appears.

**修証 shushō** — "practice-realization." Not practice then later realization; one compound.

**迷 / 悟 mei / go** — delusion / awakening as modes of relation to the myriad dharmas.

unit_label: To Study the Self Is to Forget the Self
title: To Study the Self Is to Forget the Self
sanskrit_devanagari:
仏道をならう、というは、自己をならうなり。
自己をならう、というは、自己をわするるなり。
自己をわするる、というは、万法に証せらるるなり。
万法に証せらるる、というは、自己の身心、および、他己の身心をして、脱落せしむるなり。
悟跡の休歇なるあり。
休歇なる悟跡を長長出ならしむ。
sanskrit_iast: See Original.
translation_literal: To study the Buddha Way is to study the self. To study the self is to forget the self. To forget the self is to be verified by the myriad dharmas. To be verified by the myriad dharmas is to drop away body and mind of self and other. There is a trace of realization that cannot be grasped. We continuously unfold that ungraspable trace.
commentary:
The famous ladder is not psychology alone but ontology: study becomes forgetting becomes verification becomes dropping away. The contested claim is that forgetting is not amnesia but loss of the self as center of gravity. The ungraspable trace keeps the path from becoming a possessed achievement. Existentially: each time you "get it," ask what still remains as a held identity — and let the myriad things verify you instead.

Key Terms

**自己をわするる** — "to forget the self." Not erase experience; decenter the owner.

**脱落 datsuraku** — "drop away." Body-mind of self and other fall off as clung structures.

**Meister Eckhart, *Von Abegescheidenheit* (immovable hinge / emptying):** Both refuse a spirituality of accumulation.
*Divergence:* Eckhart empties for God's occupancy; Dōgen's forgetting is verified by the myriad dharmas.

**Zhuangzi (forgetting the self / useless tree):** Both loosen fixed self-measure.
*Divergence:* Zhuangzi often ends in spontaneous ease; Dōgen binds forgetting to practice-realization.
insight: The famous ladder is not psychology alone but ontology: study becomes forgetting becomes verification becomes dropping away.
practice: Read the passage once slowly aloud. Sit three minutes without using it to improve a self-story. Then write one sentence: what verified me just now?

unit_label: The Shore Does Not Move — You Mistake the Boat
title: The Shore Does Not Move — You Mistake the Boat
sanskrit_devanagari:
人、はじめて法をもとむるとき、はるかに法の辺際を離却せり。
法、すでに、おのれに正伝するとき、すみやかに本分人なり。
人、舟にのりてゆくに、目をめぐらして、きしをみれば、きしのうつる、とあやまる。
めをしたしく、ふねにつくれば、ふねのすすむをしるがごとく、身心を乱想して万法を弁肯するには、自心自性は常住なるか？　とあやまる。
もし行李をしたしくして箇裏に帰すれば、万法のわれにあらぬ道理あきらけし。
sanskrit_iast: See Original.
translation_literal: When you first seek the dharma, you are far from its environs. When the dharma is correctly transmitted to you, you are immediately your original person. When you ride a boat and look at the shore, you may mistakenly think the shore is moving. But when you keep your eyes closely on the boat, you know the boat moves. Likewise, when you confuse body and mind and discern the myriad dharmas, you mistakenly think mind and nature are permanent. If you practice intimately and return here, the truth that the myriad dharmas are without self is clear.
commentary:
Seeking begins as distance; transmission collapses distance into original person. The boat image diagnoses projection: permanence attributed to mind is often the shore illusion. Existentially: where are you calling the world unstable while treating your viewpoint as fixed land?

Key Terms

**本分人** — "original person." What you are when dharma is transmitted, not manufactured.

**常住** — "permanence." The error of attributing fixity to self while seeing flux only outside.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Meister Eckhart, *Von Abegescheidenheit* (immovable hinge / emptying):** Both refuse a spirituality of accumulation.
*Divergence:* Eckhart empties for God's occupancy; Dōgen's forgetting is verified by the myriad dharmas.

**Zhuangzi (forgetting the self / useless tree):** Both loosen fixed self-measure.
*Divergence:* Zhuangzi often ends in spontaneous ease; Dōgen binds forgetting to practice-realization.
insight: Seeking begins as distance; transmission collapses distance into original person.
practice: Read the passage once slowly aloud. Sit three minutes without using it to improve a self-story. Then write one sentence: what verified me just now?

unit_label: Firewood Does Not Become Ash — Each Abides in Its Dharma-Position
title: Firewood Does Not Become Ash — Each Abides in Its Dharma-Position
sanskrit_devanagari:
たきぎは、はいとなる。
さらに、かえりて、たきぎとなるべきにあらず。
しかあるを、灰はのち、薪はさき、と見取すべからず。
しるべし。
薪は薪の法位に住して、さきあり、のちあり。
前後ありといえども、前後際断せり。
灰は灰の法位にありて、後あり、先あり。
かの薪、はいとなりぬるのち、さらに薪とならざるがごとく、人のしぬるのち、さらに生とならず。
しかあるを、生の、死になる、といわざるは仏法のさだまれるならいなり。
このゆえに、不生という。
死の、生にならざる、法輪のさだまれる仏転なり。
このゆえに、不滅という。
生も一時のくらいなり。
死も一時のくらいなり。
たとえば冬と春とのごとし。
冬の、春となる、とおもはず。
春の、夏となる、といわぬなり。
sanskrit_iast: See Original.
translation_literal: Firewood becomes ash. It does not become firewood again. Yet do not suppose that ash is after and firewood before. Know that firewood abides in the dharma-position of firewood, with before and after. Though there is before and after, before and after are cut off. Ash abides in the dharma-position of ash, with after and before. Just as firewood does not return to firewood after becoming ash, after death one does not return to birth. Therefore in the Buddha-dharma it is said birth does not become death — thus unborn. Death does not become birth — thus undying. Birth is a temporary position; death is a temporary position — like winter and spring. Do not think winter becomes spring, or say spring becomes summer.
commentary:
Dōgen blocks linear metaphysics of becoming that would make death a phase of a continuous self-substance. Each moment abides fully in its dharma-position; before/after are cut off even as sequence appears. Existentially: stop treating this moment as raw material for a later self; inhabit its position.

Key Terms

**法位 hōi** — "dharma-position." The complete standing of a thing as itself.

**前後際断** — "before and after cut off." Discontinuity within apparent sequence.

**Meister Eckhart, *Von Abegescheidenheit* (immovable hinge / emptying):** Both refuse a spirituality of accumulation.
*Divergence:* Eckhart empties for God's occupancy; Dōgen's forgetting is verified by the myriad dharmas.

**Zhuangzi (forgetting the self / useless tree):** Both loosen fixed self-measure.
*Divergence:* Zhuangzi often ends in spontaneous ease; Dōgen binds forgetting to practice-realization.
insight: Dōgen blocks linear metaphysics of becoming that would make death a phase of a continuous self-substance.

しかあるを、灰はのち、薪はさき、と見取すべからず。
しるべし。
薪は薪の法位に住して、さきあり、のちあり。
前後ありといえども、前後際断せり。
灰は灰の法位にありて、後あり、先あり。
かの薪、はいとなりぬるのち、さらに薪とならざるがごとく、人のしぬるのち、さらに生とならず。

このゆえに、不生という。
死の、生にならざる、法輪のさだまれる仏転なり。
このゆえに、不滅という。
生も一時のくらいなり。
死も一時のくらいなり。
たとえば冬と春とのごとし。
冬の、春となる、とおもはず。
春の、夏となる、といわぬなり。

pratibha_layers.body: See Original; key terms in commentary.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Translation
pratibha_layers.body: Firewood becomes ash. It does not become firewood again. Yet do not suppose that ash is after and firewood before. Know that firewood abides in the dharma-position of firewood, with before and after. Though there is before and after, before and after are cut off. Ash abides in the dharma-position of ash, with after and before. Just as firewood does not return to firewood after becoming ash, after death one does not return to birth. Therefore in the Buddha-dharma it is said birth does not become death — thus unborn. Death does not become birth — thus undying. Birth is a temporary position; death is a temporary position — like winter and spring. Do not think winter becomes spring, or say spring becomes summer.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Commentary
pratibha_layers.body:
Dōgen blocks linear metaphysics of becoming that would make death a phase of a continuous self-substance. Each moment abides fully in its dharma-position; before/after are cut off even as sequence appears. Existentially: stop treating this moment as raw material for a later self; inhabit its position.

**法位 hōi** — "dharma-position." The complete standing of a thing as itself.

**前後際断** — "before and after cut off." Discontinuity within apparent sequence.

**Meister Eckhart, *Von Abegescheidenheit* (immovable hinge / emptying):** Both refuse a spirituality of accumulation.
*Divergence:* Eckhart empties for God's occupancy; Dōgen's forgetting is verified by the myriad dharmas.

**Zhuangzi (forgetting the self / useless tree):** Both loosen fixed self-measure.
*Divergence:* Zhuangzi often ends in spontaneous ease; Dōgen binds forgetting to practice-realization.

unit_label: Moon in Water — Awakening Does Not Break the Person
title: Moon in Water — Awakening Does Not Break the Person
sanskrit_devanagari:
人の悟をうる、水に月のやどるがごとし。
月もぬれず( or 月ぬれず)。
水もやぶれず( or 水やぶれず)。
ひろく、おおきなる光にてあれど、尺寸の水にやどり、全月も弥天も、くさの露にもやどり、一滴の水にもやどる。
悟の、人をやぶらざること、月の、水をうがたざるがごとし。
人の、悟を罣礙せざること、滴露の天月を罣礙せざるがごとし。
ふかきことは、たかき分量なるべし。
時節の長短は、大水、小水を𢮦点し、天月の広、狭を弁取すべし。
身心に法いまだ参飽せざるには、法すでに、たれり、とおぼゆ。
法もし身心に充足すれば、ひとかたは、たらず、とおぼゆるなり。
たとえば、
船にのりて山なき海中にいでて四方をみるに、ただ、まろにのみ、みゆ。
さらに、ことなる相みゆることなし。
しかあれど、
この大海まろなるにあらず。
方なるにあらず。
のこれる海徳つくすべからざるなり。
宮殿のごとし。
瓔珞のごとし。
ただ、わがまなこのおよぶところ、しばらく、まろにみゆるのみなり。
かれがごとく、万法もまた、しかあり。
塵中格外おおく様子を帯せりといえども、参学眼力のおよぶばかりを見取、会取するなり。
万法の家風をきかんには、方、円とみゆるよりほかに、のこりの海徳、山徳おおく、きわまりなく、よもの世界あることをしるべし。
かたわらのみ、かくのごとく、あるにあらず。
直下も、一滴も、しかある、としるべし。
sanskrit_iast: See Original.
translation_literal: Realization is like the moon reflected in water. The moon does not get wet; the water is not broken. Though the light is wide and great, it lodges in a small bit of water; the whole moon and even the whole sky lodge in a dewdrop. Realization does not break a person as the moon does not pierce water. A person does not obstruct realization as a dewdrop does not obstruct the heavens' moon. Depth is the measure of the height. Investigate the length of time through the large and small of water, and discern the breadth of moon and sky.
commentary:
Awakening is intimate without violence — reflection without rupture. The contested fear that realization annihilates the person is refused; so is the fear that the person blocks realization. Existentially: stop treating insight as either self-destruction or self-possession; let it lodge like moonlight.

**悟 go** — realization as lodging, not conquest.

**罣礙** — "obstruction." Neither moon nor water finally obstructs the other.

*Divergence:* Eckhart empties for God's occupancy; Dōgen's forgetting is verified by the myriad dharmas.

**Zhuangzi (forgetting the self / useless tree):** Both loosen fixed self-measure.
*Divergence:* Zhuangzi often ends in spontaneous ease; Dōgen binds forgetting to practice-realization.
insight: Awakening is intimate without violence — reflection without rupture.
practice: Read the passage once slowly aloud. Sit three minutes without using it to improve a self-story. Then write one sentence: what verified me just now?

unit_label: Fish and Birds — Life Is the Element You Do Not Leave
title: Fish and Birds — Life Is the Element You Do Not Leave
sanskrit_devanagari:
魚の、水を行に、ゆけども水のきわなく、鳥、そらをとぶに、とぶといえども、そらのきわ、なし。
しかあれども、魚、鳥いまだ、むかしより、みず、そらをはなれず。
ただ、用大のときは、使大なり。
要小( or 用小)のときは、使小なり。
かくのごとくして、頭頭に辺際をつくさずということなく、所所に踏翻せずということなし、といえども、鳥もし、そらをいづれば、たちまちに死す。
魚もし水をいづれば、たちまちに死す。
以水為命、しりぬべし。
以空為命、しりぬべし。
以鳥為命、あり。
以魚為命、あり。
以命為鳥、なるべし。
以命為魚、なるべし。
このほか、さらに進歩あるべし。
修、証あり、その寿者命者あること、かくのごとし。
しかあるを、水をきわめ、そらをきわめてのち、水、そらをゆかん、と擬する鳥、魚あらんは、水にも、そらにも、みちをうべからず。
ところをうべからず。
このところをうれば、この行李したがいて現成公案す。
このみちをうれば、この行李したがいて現成公案なり。
このみち、このところ、
大にあらず。小にあらず。
自にあらず。他にあらず。
さきよりあるにあらず。
いま現ずるにあらざるがゆえに、かくのごとく、あるなり。
しかあるがごとく、人もし仏道を修、証するに、
得一法、通一法なり。
遇一行、修一行なり。
これに、ところあり、みち通達せるによりて、しらるるきわの、しるからざるは、このしることの、仏法の究尽と同生し同参するゆえに、しかあるなり。
得所かならず自己の知見となりて慮知にしられんずる、とならうことなかれ。
証究すみやかに現成すといえども、密有かならずしも見成にあらず。
見成、これ、何必なり。
sanskrit_iast: See Original.
translation_literal: When fish swim in water, however far they go the water has no end. When birds fly in sky, however far they fly the sky has no end. Yet fish and birds have never left water or sky. When need is great, use is great; when need is small, use is small. They use each place to the full and turn each thing freely — yet if a bird leaves the sky it dies at once; if a fish leaves water it dies at once. Know that water is life; sky is life. Bird is life; fish is life. Life is bird; life is fish. Practice-realization is like this. If a bird or fish tried to go through sky or water after first exhausting them, it would find neither path nor place. When you find this place, practice actualizes the koan here. When you find this path, practice actualizes the koan on this path. This place, this path, is neither large nor small, self nor other, already there nor appearing now — therefore it is thus.
commentary:
You cannot first finish the element then travel it; practice is swimming, not surveying the ocean from outside. Finding place and path is genjōkōan — the absolute matter actualized as this activity. Existentially: stop postponing practice until conditions are "understood"; the element is already the path.

Key Terms

**現成公案** — actualized as this place/path.

**行李 angya/angya as practice-activity** — the walking of the Way as use of the element.

**Meister Eckhart, *Von Abegescheidenheit* (immovable hinge / emptying):** Both refuse a spirituality of accumulation.
*Divergence:* Eckhart empties for God's occupancy; Dōgen's forgetting is verified by the myriad dharmas.

**Zhuangzi (forgetting the self / useless tree):** Both loosen fixed self-measure.
*Divergence:* Zhuangzi often ends in spontaneous ease; Dōgen binds forgetting to practice-realization.
insight: You cannot first finish the element then travel it; practice is swimming, not surveying the ocean from outside.

unit_label: The Twelve Hours Are Not Measured — Yet They Are Time
title: The Twelve Hours Are Not Measured — Yet They Are Time
sanskrit_devanagari:
いわゆる、有時は、時、すでに、これ、有なり。
有はみな、時なり。
丈六金身、これ、時なり。
時なるがゆえに、時の荘厳、光明あり。
いまの十二時に習学すべし。
三頭八臂、これ、時なり。
時なるがゆえに、いまの十二時に一如なるべし。
十二時の長遠短促、いまだ度量せずといえども、これを十二時という。
去来の方跡あきらかなるによりて、人、これを疑著せず。
疑著せざれども、しれるにあらず。
衆生、もとより、しらざる毎物毎事を疑著すること一定せざるがゆえに、疑著する前程、かならずしも、いまの疑著に符合することなし。
ただ、疑著、しばらく、時なるのみなり。
sanskrit_iast: See Original.
translation_literal: So-called being-time means that time already is being, and all being is time. The sixteen-foot golden body is time; because it is time, it has time's adornment and radiance. We have not yet measured the long and short of the twelve hours, yet we call them twelve hours. People do not doubt them because coming-and-going traces seem clear — yet not doubting is not knowing.
commentary:

unit_label: Array the Self as the Whole World — Each Thing Is a Time
title: Array the Self as the Whole World — Each Thing Is a Time
sanskrit_devanagari:
われを排列しおきて尽界とせり。
この尽界の頭頭、物物を時時なりと覰見すべし。
物物の、相礙せざるは、時時の、相礙せざるがごとし。
このゆえに、同時発心あり、同心発時あり。
および、修行、成道も、かくのごとし。
われを排列して、われ、これをみるなり。
自己の、時なる道理、それ、かくのごとし。
恁麼の道理なるゆえに、尽地に万象、百草あり。
一草、一象、おのおの、尽地にあることを参学すべし。
かくのごとくの( or この)往来は修行の発足なり。
到、恁麼の田地のとき、すなわち、一草、一象なり。
会、象、不会、象なり。
会、草、不会、草なり。
正当恁麼時のみなるがゆえに、有時みな、尽時なり。
有草、有象ともに時なり。
時時の時に尽有、尽界あるなり。
しばらく、いまの時にもれたる尽有、尽界ありや？　なしや？　と観想すべし。
sanskrit_iast: See Original.
translation_literal: We set the self out in array and make that the whole world. See each thing of this whole world as a time. Things do not hinder one another, just as times do not hinder one another. Therefore there is arising of mind at the same time, and arising of time at the same mind. Practice and realization are also like this. We set the self out in array and see that. The reason the self is time is like this.
commentary:
The self is not a private capsule inside time; arrayed, it is the world as times. Non-hindrance of things mirrors non-hindrance of times. Existentially: when you feel time as enemy of the self, check whether you have refused to array the self as world.

**排列** — "array / arrange." The self set out as world.

**相礙せざる** — non-hindrance of things and times.

**Meister Eckhart, *Von Abegescheidenheit* (immovable hinge / emptying):** Both refuse a spirituality of accumulation.
*Divergence:* Eckhart empties for God's occupancy; Dōgen's forgetting is verified by the myriad dharmas.

**Zhuangzi (forgetting the self / useless tree):** Both loosen fixed self-measure.
*Divergence:* Zhuangzi often ends in spontaneous ease; Dōgen binds forgetting to practice-realization.
insight: The self is not a private capsule inside time; arrayed, it is the world as times.
practice: Read the passage once slowly aloud. Sit three minutes without using it to improve a self-story. Then write one sentence: what verified me just now?

unit_label: Yesterday's Mountains Are Not Gone — Being-Time Is Right Now
title: Yesterday's Mountains Are Not Gone — Being-Time Is Right Now
sanskrit_devanagari:
しかあるを、仏法をならわざる凡夫の時節に、あらゆる見解は、有時のことばをきくに、おもわく、あるときは三頭八臂となれりき、あるときは丈六八尺となれりき、たとえば、河をすぎ、山をすぎしがごとくなり。と。
いまは、その山河、たとえ、あるらめども、われ、すぎきたりて、いまは玉殿、朱楼に処せり。山河と、われと、天と、地と、なり。と、おもう。
しかあれども、道理、この一条のみにあらず。
いわゆる、山をのぼり、河をわたりし時に、われありき。
われに時あるべし。
われ、すでにあり。
時、さるべからず。
時もし去来の相にならずば、上山の時は有時の而今なり。
時もし去来の相を保任せば、われに有時の而今ある。
これ、有時なり。
かの上山、渡河の時、この玉殿、朱楼の時を呑却せざらんや？　吐却せざらんや？
三頭八臂は、きのうの時なり。
丈六八尺は、きょうの時なり。
しかあれども、その昨今の道理、ただ、これ、山のなかに直入して千峯、万峯をみわたす時節なり。
すぎぬるにあらず。
三頭八臂も、すなわち、わが有時にて一経す。
彼方にあるににたれども、而今なり。
丈六八尺も、すなわち、わが有時にて一経す。
彼所にあるににたれども、而今なり。
しかあれば、松も時なり。
竹も時なり。
sanskrit_iast: See Original.
translation_literal: Ordinary people hearing "being-time" think: there was a time I was three heads and eight arms, a time I was the golden body — like crossing rivers and mountains. Now those mountains and rivers seem to exist, but I have passed them and dwell in a jeweled palace — heaven and earth are separate from me. But this is not the only line. At the time of climbing mountains and crossing rivers, there was I; there should be time in me. I already am; time should not depart. If time does not have the form of coming and going, the time of climbing is the immediate now of being-time. Even if time seems to come and go, the immediate now of being-time is in me. Those mountains and rivers of that time — does this jeweled-palace time swallow them or spit them out? Three heads and eight arms are yesterday's time; the golden body is today's time — yet yesterday and today are just looking across a thousand peaks. They have not passed. Even three heads, seeming over there, are right now as my being-time.
commentary:
The ordinary narrative of time-as-departure is refused. Past forms are not discarded husks; they are being-time still. Existentially: stop exiling former selves as "over"; meet them as right-now being-time without nostalgia's possession.

Key Terms

**而今 nikon** — "immediate now."

**去来** — coming-and-going as the false form attributed to time.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Meister Eckhart, *Von Abegescheidenheit* (immovable hinge / emptying):** Both refuse a spirituality of accumulation.
*Divergence:* Eckhart empties for God's occupancy; Dōgen's forgetting is verified by the myriad dharmas.

**Zhuangzi (forgetting the self / useless tree):** Both loosen fixed self-measure.
*Divergence:* Zhuangzi often ends in spontaneous ease; Dōgen binds forgetting to practice-realization.
insight: The ordinary narrative of time-as-departure is refused.
practice: Read the passage once slowly aloud. Sit three minutes without using it to improve a self-story. Then write one sentence: what verified me just now?

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Commentary
pratibha_layers.body:
The ordinary narrative of time-as-departure is refused. Past forms are not discarded husks; they are being-time still. Existentially: stop exiling former selves as "over"; meet them as right-now being-time without nostalgia's possession.

Key Terms

**而今 nikon** — "immediate now."

**去来** — coming-and-going as the false form attributed to time.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Meister Eckhart, *Von Abegescheidenheit* (immovable hinge / emptying):** Both refuse a spirituality of accumulation.
*Divergence:* Eckhart empties for God's occupancy; Dōgen's forgetting is verified by the myriad dharmas.

**Zhuangzi (forgetting the self / useless tree):** Both loosen fixed self-measure.
*Divergence:* Zhuangzi often ends in spontaneous ease; Dōgen binds forgetting to practice-realization.

unit_label: Time Does Not Merely Fly Away — Passage Is Time's Virtue
title: Time Does Not Merely Fly Away — Passage Is Time's Virtue
sanskrit_devanagari:
時は飛去するとのみ解会すべからず。
飛去は時の能とのみは学すべからず。
時もし飛去に一任せば、間隙、ありぬべし。
有時の道を経聞せざるは、すぎぬる、とのみ学するによりてなり。
要をとりて、いわば、
尽界に、あらゆる尽有は、つらなりながら時時なり。
有時なるによりて、吾、有時なり。
有時に(は)経歴の功徳あり。
いわゆる、
今日より明日に経歴す。
今日より昨日に経歴す。
昨日より今日に経歴す。
今日より今日に経歴す。
明日より明日に経歴す。
経歴は、それ、時の功徳なるがゆえに。
古今の時、かさなれるにあらず、ならびつもれるにあらざれども、青原も時なり、黄檗も時なり、江西も石頭も時なり。
自他、すでに時なるがゆえに、修、証は諸時なり。
入泥入水、おなじく、時なり。
いまの凡夫の見、および、見の因縁、これ、凡夫のみるところなりといえども、凡夫の法にあらず。
法、しばらく、凡夫を因縁せるのみなり。
この時、この有は、法にあらず、と学するがゆえに、丈六金身は、われにあらず、と認ずるなり。
われを丈六金身にあらずとのがれんとする、また、すなわち、有時の片片なり。
未証拠者の看看なり。
いま、世界に排列せる、うま、ひつじをあらしむるも、住法位の恁麼なる昇降、上下なり。
ねずみも時なり。
とらも時なり。
生も時なり。
仏も時なり。
この時、三頭八臂にて尽界を証し、丈六金身にて尽界を証す。
それ、尽界をもって尽界を界尽するを、究尽する、とはいうなり。
丈六金身をもって丈六金身するを、発心、修行、菩提、涅槃と現成する、すなわち、有なり、時なり。
尽時を尽有と究尽するのみ。
さらに剰法なし。剰法、これ、剰法なるがゆえに。
たとえ半究尽の有時も、半有時の究尽なり。
たとえ、蹉過す、と、みゆる形段も、有なり。
さらに、かれにまかすれば、蹉過の現成する前後ながら、有時の住位なり。
住法位の活鱍鱍地なる、これ、有時なり。
無と動著すべからず。
有と強為すべからず。
時は一向にすぐる、とのみ計功して、未到と解会せず。
解会は時なりといえども、他にひかるる縁なし。
去来と認じて、住位の有時と見徹せる皮袋なし。
いわんや、透関の時あらんや？
たとえ住位を認ずとも、だれが既得、恁麼の保任を道得せん？
たとえ恁麼と道得せること、ひさしきも、いまだ面目、現前を模索せざるなし。
凡夫の有時なるに一任すれば、菩提、涅槃も、わずかに去来の相のみなる有時なり。
おおよそ羅籠、とどまらず、有時、現成なり。
いま、右界に現成し左方に現成する天王天衆、いまも、わが尽力する有時なり。
その余外にある水陸の衆有時、これ、わが、いま尽力して現成するなり。
冥、陽に有時なる諸類、諸頭みな、わが尽力、現成なり、尽力、経歴なり。
わが、いま尽力経歴にあらざれば、一法、一物も現成することなし、経歴することなし、と参学すべし。
経歴というは、風雨の東西するがごとく学しきたるべからず。
尽界は不動転なるにあらず、不進退なるにあらず、経歴なり。
経歴は、たとえば、春のごとし。
春に許多般の様子あり。
これを経歴という。
外物なきに経歴する、と参学すべし。
たとえば、春の経歴は、かならず、春を経歴するなり。
経歴は春にあらざれども、春の経歴なるがゆえに、経歴、いま、春の時に成道せり。
審細に参来参去すべし。
経歴をいうに、境は外頭にして、能経歴の法は東にむきて百、千世界をゆきすぎて百、千(、万)劫をふる、と、おもうは、仏道の参学、これのみを専一にせざるなり。

translation_literal: Do not understand time only as flying away. Do not study flying away as time's only capacity. If time were left only to flying away, gaps would appear. Not hearing the Way of being-time comes from studying only "it has passed." In brief: all beings of the whole world, while lined up, are times. Because it is being-time, I am being-time. Being-time has the virtue of passage: from today to tomorrow; from today to yesterday; from yesterday to today; from today to today; from tomorrow to tomorrow. Passage is time's virtue. Ancient and modern times are neither layered nor piled, yet Qingyuan is time, Huangbo is time, Jiangxi and Shitou are time. Because self and other are already time, practice-realization is many times. Even entering mud and water is time.
commentary:
Passage (*keiryaku*) is not leakage of being; it is time's functioning — including today-to-today. Ancestors are times, not figures trapped in a past drawer. Existentially: treat today's practice as passage's virtue, not as a race against disappearing time.

Key Terms

**経歴 keiryaku** — "passage / passage-through." Time's virtue, not mere loss.

**尽界尽有** — whole world / all being as times.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Meister Eckhart, *Von Abegescheidenheit* (immovable hinge / emptying):** Both refuse a spirituality of accumulation.
*Divergence:* Eckhart empties for God's occupancy; Dōgen's forgetting is verified by the myriad dharmas.

**Zhuangzi (forgetting the self / useless tree):** Both loosen fixed self-measure.
*Divergence:* Zhuangzi often ends in spontaneous ease; Dōgen binds forgetting to practice-realization.
insight: Passage (*keiryaku*) is not leakage of being; it is time's functioning — including today-to-today.

pratibha_layers.body: Do not understand time only as flying away. Do not study flying away as time's only capacity. If time were left only to flying away, gaps would appear. Not hearing the Way of being-time comes from studying only "it has passed." In brief: all beings of the whole world, while lined up, are times. Because it is being-time, I am being-time. Being-time has the virtue of passage: from today to tomorrow; from today to yesterday; from yesterday to today; from today to today; from tomorrow to tomorrow. Passage is time's virtue. Ancient and modern times are neither layered nor piled, yet Qingyuan is time, Huangbo is time, Jiangxi and Shitou are time. Because self and other are already time, practice-realization is many times. Even entering mud and water is time.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Commentary
pratibha_layers.body:
Passage (*keiryaku*) is not leakage of being; it is time's functioning — including today-to-today. Ancestors are times, not figures trapped in a past drawer. Existentially: treat today's practice as passage's virtue, not as a race against disappearing time.

Key Terms

**経歴 keiryaku** — "passage / passage-through." Time's virtue, not mere loss.

**尽界尽有** — whole world / all being as times.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Meister Eckhart, *Von Abegescheidenheit* (immovable hinge / emptying):** Both refuse a spirituality of accumulation.
*Divergence:* Eckhart empties for God's occupancy; Dōgen's forgetting is verified by the myriad dharmas.

**Zhuangzi (forgetting the self / useless tree):** Both loosen fixed self-measure.
*Divergence:* Zhuangzi often ends in spontaneous ease; Dōgen binds forgetting to practice-realization.

pratibha_layers.label: Practice
pratibha_layers.body: Read the passage once slowly aloud. Sit three minutes without using it to improve a self-story. Then write one sentence: what verified me just now?

title: The Reed Complains of Separation

بشنو این نی چون شکایت می‌کند /// از جدایی‌ها حکایت می‌کند

unit_label: Whoever Is Far from Their Origin Seeks Return

unit_label: Everyone Became My Friend from Opinion — None Sought My Secret
title: Everyone Became My Friend from Opinion — None Sought My Secret
sanskrit_devanagari:

unit_label: The Raw Cannot Grasp the Cooked — So the Word Is Short, Wa-s-salām
title: The Raw Cannot Grasp the Cooked — So the Word Is Short, Wa-s-salām
sanskrit_devanagari:
در غمِ ما روزها بیگاه شد /// روزها با سوزها همراه شد
روزها گر رفت گو رو باک نیست /// تو بمان ای آنک چون تو پاک نیست
هر که جز ماهی ز آبش سیر شد /// هرکه بی روزیست روزش دیر شد

**Milarepa (song as vehicle):** Both use song to cross what argument cannot.
*Divergence:* Milarepa's songs are often instructional; the nay is primarily ontological lament.

unit_label: Moses Hears the Shepherd's Rough Prayer
title: Moses Hears the Shepherd's Rough Prayer
source_reference: Rūmī, *Mathnawī* II, Moses and the shepherd (§1)
sanskrit_devanagari:
دید موسی یک شبانی را به راه /// کو همی‌گفت ای گزیننده اله
تو کجایی تا شوم من چاکرت /// چارقت دوزم کنم شانه سرت
جامه‌ات شویم شپشهاات کُشم /// شیر پیشت آورم ای محتشم
دستکت بوسم بمالم پایکت /// وقت خواب آید بروبم جایکت
ای فدای تو همه بزهای من /// ای بیادت هیهی و هیهای من
این نمط بیهوده می‌گفت آن شبان /// گفت موسی با کی است این ای فلان
sanskrit_iast: See Original.
translation_literal: Moses saw a shepherd on the road saying: O God who chooses — where are You, that I may become Your servant, mend Your shoe, comb Your head, wash Your clothes, kill Your lice, bring You milk, kiss Your hand, rub Your feet, sweep Your place at sleep — O all my goats are Your sacrifice…
commentary:
The shepherd's prayer is anthropomorphic, intimate, "crude." Its contested holiness is precisely that heat. Existentially: notice when your prayer becomes correct and cold.

Key Terms

**حال / قال ḥāl / qāl** — state / speech.

**سوز sūz** — burning.

**ملت عشق** — the creed/community of love.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Bhagavad Gītā 9 (even a leaf offered with devotion):** Both privilege sincere offering over formal perfection.
*Divergence:* The Gītā keeps varṇa-dharma frames; Rūmī's love-creed speaks across forms.

**Eckhart (silence / not naming detachment):** Both warn that correct speech can spoil intimacy.
*Divergence:* Eckhart's worry is exiting the ground by naming; Rūmī's is shaming the lover's tongue.
insight: The shepherd's prayer is anthropomorphic, intimate, "crude.
practice: Pray for one minute in deliberately simple, even "crude" language of care. Then sit one minute in burning without words. Notice which felt more true.

unit_label: Moses Condemns the Shepherd as Unbeliever
title: Moses Condemns the Shepherd as Unbeliever
source_reference: Rūmī, *Mathnawī* II, Moses and the shepherd (§2)
sanskrit_devanagari:
گفت با آنکس که ما را آفرید /// این زمین و چرخ ازو آمد پدید
گفت موسی های بس مُدبِر شدی /// خود مسلمان ناشده کافر شدی
این چه ژاژست این چه کفرست و فُشار /// پنبه‌ای اندر دهان خود فشار
گفت ای موسی دهانم دوختی /// وز پشیمانی تو جانم سوختی
جامه را بدرید و آهی کرد تفت /// سر نهاد اندر بیابانی و رفت
وحی آمد سوی موسی از خدا /// بندهٔ ما را ز ما کردی جدا

translation_literal: Moses said: Who are you speaking to? The shepherd: to the One who created us, earth and sphere. Moses: Stop — you have become ruined; not yet Muslim, you have become unbeliever. What nonsense, what blasphemy — stuff cotton in your mouth!

Prophetic correctness attacks living intimacy. The contested drama is orthodoxy wounding love. Existentially: where do you police others' language of God?

*Divergence:* Eckhart's worry is exiting the ground by naming; Rūmī's is shaming the lover's tongue.

title: God Rebukes Moses — You Came to Unite, Not Divide
source_reference: Rūmī, *Mathnawī* II, Moses and the shepherd (§3)

تا توانی پا مَنِه اندر فَراق /// اَبْغَضُ الْاَشْیاء عِندي الطَّلاق
هر کسی را سیرتی بنهاده‌ام /// هر کسی را اصطلاحی داده‌ام
ما بَری از پاک و ناپاکی همه /// از گِرانجانی و چالاکی همه
ما زبان را نَنْگریم و قال را /// ما روان را بنگریم و حال را
ناظرِ قلبیم اگر خاشِع بوَد /// گرچه گفتِ لَفظ، ناخاضِع رُوَد
زانک دل جَوهر بوَد، گفتن عَرَض /// پس طُفَیل آمد عَرَض، جَوهرْ غَرَض
چند ازین اَلفاظ و اِضْمار و مَجاز؟ /// سوزْ خواهمْ سوز، با آن سوزْ ساز

تا توانی پا مَنِه اندر فَراق /// اَبْغَضُ الْاَشْیاء عِندي الطَّلاق
هر کسی را سیرتی بنهاده‌ام /// هر کسی را اصطلاحی داده‌ام
ما بَری از پاک و ناپاکی همه /// از گِرانجانی و چالاکی همه
ما زبان را نَنْگریم و قال را /// ما روان را بنگریم و حال را
ناظرِ قلبیم اگر خاشِع بوَد /// گرچه گفتِ لَفظ، ناخاضِع رُوَد
زانک دل جَوهر بوَد، گفتن عَرَض /// پس طُفَیل آمد عَرَض، جَوهرْ غَرَض
چند ازین اَلفاظ و اِضْمار و مَجاز؟ /// سوزْ خواهمْ سوز، با آن سوزْ ساز
translation: The shepherd tore his cloak, sighed hot, and fled to the desert. Revelation came to Moses: You have separated Our servant from Us. Did you come to join or to split? Do not step into separation if you can help it — divorce is most hateful to Me. I have given each a way and a tongue…

abhyasa: Pray for one minute in deliberately simple, even "crude" language of care. Then sit one minute in burning without words. Notice which felt more true.

pratibha_layers.label: Pratibha Commentary
pratibha_layers.body:
God's rebuke relocates criteria from verbal purity to relational effect: unite or divide. Existentially: measure speech by whether it joins or splits lovers from the Beloved.

Key Terms

**حال / قال ḥāl / qāl** — state / speech.

**سوز sūz** — burning.

**ملت عشق** — the creed/community of love.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Bhagavad Gītā 9 (even a leaf offered with devotion):** Both privilege sincere offering over formal perfection.
*Divergence:* The Gītā keeps varṇa-dharma frames; Rūmī's love-creed speaks across forms.

**Eckhart (silence / not naming detachment):** Both warn that correct speech can spoil intimacy.
*Divergence:* Eckhart's worry is exiting the ground by naming; Rūmī's is shaming the lover's tongue.

unit_label: We Look at the Heart and the State — Not the Words
title: We Look at the Heart and the State — Not the Words
source_reference: Rūmī, *Mathnawī* II, Moses and the shepherd (§4)
sanskrit_devanagari:
آتشی از عشق در جانْ بَر فُروز /// سَر بِسَر فکر و عبارت را بسوز
ملتِ عشق از همه دینها جداست /// عاشقان را ملت و مذهب خداست
لَعْل را گر مُهر نبوَد باک نیست /// عشق در دریای غم، غمناک نیست
sanskrit_iast: See Original.
translation_literal: We do not look at tongue and speech; We look at spirit and state. If the heart is humble, even if the wording is not. The heart is substance; speech is accident. How long words and metaphors? I want burning — burn thought and expression. Kindle love's fire in the soul. The religion of love is apart from all religions; for lovers, religion and rite are God. A ruby needs no seal; love in a sea of grief is not grief-stricken.
commentary:
The climax: God reads ḥāl (state) over qāl (speech). Love's creed relativizes confessional borders without abolishing heat. Existentially: prefer one degree of burning to ten pages of correct theology.

unit_label: The Elephant in the Dark House
title: The Elephant in the Dark House
sanskrit_devanagari:
پیل اندر خانه‌ی تاریک بود /// عرضه را آورده بودندش هنود
از برای دیدنش مردم بسی /// اندر آن ظلمت همی‌شد هر کسی
دیدنش با چشم چون ممکن نبود /// اندر آن تاریکیش کف می‌بسود
sanskrit_iast: See Original.
translation_literal: An elephant was in a dark house — Indians had brought it for display. Many people went into that darkness to see it. Since seeing with the eye was impossible, each felt it with the palm in the dark.
commentary:
Fragmentary knowledge begins in darkness mistaken for vision. The contested setup is epistemic: when the whole is present but unlit, touch substitutes for seeing and manufactures certainty. Existentially: name one domain where you are still groping parts while claiming to know the animal.

Key Terms

**پیل pīl** — elephant; the whole Reality/Truth.

**خانه‌ی تاریک** — dark house; the condition of unillumined perception.

**کف kaf** — palm; limited sense-grasp.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Plato, cave (Republic VII):** Both stage partial perception as mistaking part for whole.
*Divergence:* Plato's exit is dialectic toward Forms; Rūmī's remedy is the candle / Sea-eye of unveiling.

**Nagarjuna (emptiness of views):** Both puncture clinging to partial descriptions.
*Divergence:* Madhyamaka empties views dialectically; Rūmī empties them by light and oceanic seeing.
insight: Fragmentary knowledge begins in darkness mistaken for vision.
practice: Today, when you form a strong opinion of a person or situation, pause and say: I am touching one part in the dark. Name what part, and what you have not touched.

provenance.edition: Persian: masnavi.net / Ganjoor tradition; Nicholson PD English consulted; Pratibha English editorial (UNVERIFIED)

unit_label: Trunk, Ear, Leg, Back — Each Names a Different Elephant
title: Trunk, Ear, Leg, Back — Each Names a Different Elephant
sanskrit_devanagari:
آن یکی را کف به خرطوم اوفتاد /// گفت همچون ناودانست این نهاد
آن یکی را دست بر گوشش رسید /// آن برو چون بادبیزن شد پدید
آن یکی را کف چو بر پایش بسود /// گفت شکل پیل دیدم چون عمود
آن یکی بر پشت او بنهاد دست /// گفت خود این پیل چون تختی بدست
همچنین هر یک به جزوی که رسید /// فهم آن می‌کرد هر جا می‌شنید
از نظرگه گفتشان شد مختلف /// آن یکی دالش لقب داد این الف
sanskrit_iast: See Original.
translation_literal: One's palm fell on the trunk — "This being is like a water-spout." Another's hand reached the ear — it seemed a fan. Another felt the leg — "I found the elephant's shape like a pillar." Another laid a hand on the back — "Truly this elephant is like a throne." Each understood according to the part touched. Their words differed by viewpoint: one nicknamed it *dāl*, another *alif*.
commentary:
Conflict is often not about different elephants but different grips. The contested pastoral use is irenic without relativism: disagreement is explained by *naẓargāh* (viewing-place), not by denying a whole. Existentially: in your next argument, ask what part each hand is on.

Key Terms

**جزو juzʾ** — part; the fragment mistaken for the whole.

**نظرگه naẓargāh** — viewing-place; the stand that shapes speech.

**دال / الف** — letter-shapes as rival nicknames for one animal.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Jain anekāntavāda (many-sidedness):** Both honor partial standpoints.
*Divergence:* Jain thought systematizes standpoints; Rūmī presses toward a shared light that ends quarrel.

**Zhuangzi (pipes of heaven / each thing its own right):** Both relativize forced consensus.
*Divergence:* Zhuangzi often rests in perspectival ease; Rūmī wants the candle that ends difference.
insight: Conflict is often not about different elephants but different grips.
practice: Write two opposing descriptions of the same hard situation as if each were a palm on a different limb. Do not pick a winner. Sit one minute with the elephant still dark.

provenance.edition: Persian: masnavi.net / Ganjoor tradition; Nicholson PD English consulted; Pratibha English editorial (UNVERIFIED)

unit_label: If Each Had a Candle — Leave Foam, See with the Sea's Eye
title: If Each Had a Candle — Leave Foam, See with the Sea's Eye
sanskrit_devanagari:
در کف هر کس اگر شمعی بدی /// اختلاف از گفتشان بیرون شدی
چشم حس همچون کف دستست و بس /// نیست کف را بر همه‌ی او دست‌رس
چشم دریا دیگرست و کف دگر /// کف بهل وز دیده‌ی دریا نگر
جنبش کفها ز دریا روز و شب /// کف همی‌بینی و دریا نه عجب
ما چو کشتیها بهم بر می‌زنیم /// تیره‌چشمیم و در آب روشنیم
ای تو در کشتی تن رفته به خواب /// آب را دیدی نگر در آب آب
آب را آبیست کو می‌راندش /// روح را روحیست کو می‌خواندش
sanskrit_iast: See Original.
translation_literal: If each had held a candle, difference would have left their speech. The sense-eye is only a palm — the palm cannot reach the whole. The Sea's eye is one thing, foam another: leave the foam and look with the Sea's eye. Foam moves from the Sea day and night — you see foam, not Sea: marvel! We collide like boats, dark-eyed though in clear water. O you asleep in the body's boat — you have seen water; look at the Water of water. Water has a Water that drives it; spirit has a Spirit that calls it.
commentary:
The candle is shared illumination; the Sea's eye is a different organ than sense. Nested waters and spirits refuse stopping at the first layer. Existentially: stop polishing foam-arguments; ask for the seeing that makes quarrel unnecessary.

Key Terms

**شمع shamʿ** — candle; shared light ending quarrel.

**چشم دریا** — Sea's eye; non-partial vision.

**آب آب** — Water of water; source within source.

**روح را روحی** — a Spirit calling the spirit.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Plotinus (One beyond intellect / nested procession):** Both push past surface seeing.
*Divergence:* Plotinus's ascent is contemplative stripping; Rūmī's images stay narrative and oceanic.

**Eckhart (empty for God's writing):** Both require a cleared receptive organ.
*Divergence:* Eckhart's blank tablet is readiness; Rūmī's candle is communal illumination of one elephant.
insight: The candle is shared illumination; the Sea's eye is a different organ than sense.
practice: In silence for five minutes, each time a partial judgment arises, whisper: foam. Return to breath as if looking for the Water of water.

provenance.edition: Persian: masnavi.net / Ganjoor tradition; Nicholson PD English consulted; Pratibha English editorial (UNVERIFIED)

unit_label: Chinese Colour, Greek Polish — From Many Colours to Colourlessness
title: Chinese Colour, Greek Polish — From Many Colours to Colourlessness
sanskrit_devanagari:
چینیان گفتند ما نقاش‌تر /// رومیان گفتند ما را کر و فر
چینیان صد رنگ از شه خواستند /// پس خزینه باز کرد آن ارجمند
رومیان گفتند نی نقش و نه رنگ /// در خور آید کار را جز دفع زنگ
در فرو بستند و صیقل می‌زدند /// همچو گردون ساده و صافی شدند
از دو صد رنگی به بی‌رنگی رهی است /// رنگ چون ابر است و بی‌رنگی مهی است
هر چه اندر ابر ضو بینی و تاب /// آن ز اختر دان و ماه و آفتاب
sanskrit_iast: See Original.
translation_literal: The Chinese said, "We are the better painters"; the Greeks said, "Excellence and power are ours." The Chinese asked the king for a hundred colours; the treasury opened. The Greeks said, "Neither design nor colour is fit for our work — only removing rust." They shut the door and burnished, becoming clear and pure as the sky. There is a way from two hundred colours to colourlessness: colour is cloud; colourlessness is moon. Whatever light you see in cloud comes from star, moon, and sun.
commentary:
Two spiritual technologies: accumulation of forms vs polishing the receptacle. The contested claim is that colourlessness is not blankness but maximal receptivity — moon receiving light. Existentially: are you adding more colours to the room, or removing rust?

Key Terms

**صیقل ṣayqal** — burnishing/polish; Sufi purification of the breast.

**بی‌رنگی** — colourlessness; the clear mirror-state.

**دفع زنگ** — removing rust; clearing the heart's tarnish.

Cross-Tradition Resonances

**Pratyabhijñāhṛdayam (recognition vs accumulation):** Both privilege clearing over adding content.
*Divergence:* Recognition reclaims authorship of display; Rūmī's Greeks become mirrors of another's art.

**Dōgen (forgetting the self):** Both empty the clutching subject.
*Divergence:* Dōgen's forgetting is verified by myriad dharmas; Rūmī's polish mirrors painted forms more beautifully.
insight: Two spiritual technologies: accumulation of forms vs polishing the receptacle.
practice: Choose one habit of spiritual "colour collecting" (books, opinions, techniques). For one day, practice only rust-removal: drop one reactive pattern each time it appears.

provenance.edition: Persian: masnavi.net / Ganjoor tradition; Nicholson PD English consulted; Pratibha English editorial (UNVERIFIED)
